Authenticate deployed agents with OIDC ​

A deployed Agent SDK agent can mint short-lived OIDC JWTs signed by Cursor and exchange them for temporary cloud credentials or service tokens without storing static access keys in deployment secrets.

Agent SDK tokens share the https://api.cursor.com issuer, discovery endpoints, signing keys, 5-minute lifetime, socket path, and per-pod rate limits documented in Cloud Agents OIDC tokens. They differ in four ways:

AspectCloud AgentsAgent SDK deployments
Audience allowlistAny valid aud stringMust be declared in hosting.oidc.audiences; undeclared audiences return HTTP 400.
Subject (sub)cloud_agent_id:<id> (or projected team_id:<id> via sub_claim)Always agent_sdk_deployment_id:<deployment-id>. Sending sub_claim returns HTTP 400.
Runtime claim (agent_runtime)"managed" or "self_hosted""agent_sdk".
Additional claimsIncludes owner, team, repository, branch, and turn claimsSee Token claims. No owner, team, repository, or session claims.

Declare allowed audiences ​

A deployed agent can only mint tokens for audiences declared in hosting.oidc.audiences in bot/agent.ts. If you omit hosting.oidc.audiences, every mint request fails with HTTP 400.

ts
// bot/agent.ts
import { defineAgent } from "@grok/agent-sdk";

export default defineAgent({
  hosting: {
    egressDomains: ["sts.amazonaws.com"],
    oidc: {
      audiences: ["sts.amazonaws.com"],
    },
  },
});

Minting talks to a local Unix socket, so minting itself needs no egress entry. Calling the relying party to exchange the token still requires its hostname in hosting.egressDomains, such as sts.amazonaws.com (and any AWS service host your agent calls afterward).

Audience rules:

  • List exact audience strings only. Wildcards (*) are rejected.
  • Declare at most 8 audiences per deployment.
  • Each audience must be 1 to 512 printable ASCII characters with no spaces or control characters.
  • Cursor-reserved audiences (such as cursor.com hosts) are rejected at deploy time and at mint time.
  • Cursor saves hosting.oidc.audiences when you deploy. Redeploy to add or remove an audience.

Mint a token with getOidcToken ​

Import getOidcToken from @grok/agent-sdk and call it inside a tool, channel handler, or callback when your agent needs a token.

ts
// bot/tools/assume_aws_role.ts
import { getOidcToken, OidcTokenError } from "@grok/agent-sdk";
import { defineTool } from "@grok/agent-sdk/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineTool({
  description: "Exchange an OIDC token for temporary AWS credentials.",
  inputSchema: z.object({}),
  async execute() {
    let token: string;
    try {
      const result = await getOidcToken("sts.amazonaws.com");
      token = result.token;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof OidcTokenError) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          code: error.code,
          status: error.status ?? null,
          reason: error.reason ?? null,
        };
      }
      throw error;
    }

    const body = new URLSearchParams({
      Action: "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
      Version: "2011-06-15",
      RoleArn: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/my-agent-role",
      RoleSessionName: "agent-sdk-session",
      WebIdentityToken: token,
    });

    const response = await fetch("https://sts.amazonaws.com/", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
        accept: "application/json",
      },
      body,
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      return { ok: false, stsStatus: response.status };
    }
    return { ok: true };
  },
});

Call getOidcToken inside a tool, handler, or callback, not at module load time.

Return value and caching ​

getOidcToken(audience: string) returns Promise<OidcToken>:

FieldTypeMeaning
tokenstringCompact RS256-signed JWT. Never log it.
expiresAtDateToken expiration timestamp from the socket's expires_at field.

getOidcToken caches one token per audience in memory and refreshes it 60 seconds before expiresAt. Concurrent callers for the same audience share a single in-flight mint request. Each mint request times out after 20 seconds.

Error handling ​

getOidcToken throws OidcTokenError (a subclass of Error with name === "OidcTokenError") on failure:

FieldTypeMeaning
codeOidcTokenErrorCodeFailure category listed below.
statusnumber | undefinedHTTP status code from the identity socket when an HTTP response was received.
reasonstring | undefinedMachine-readable error string from the socket's JSON error body, when present.

OidcTokenErrorCode values:

codeTypical statusCauseWhat to do
"not_hosted"undefinedNo identity socket exists (for example, during local agent-sdk dev or agent-sdk serve).Use local credentials in development or skip OIDC locally.
"refused"403The deployment is not running (stopped or deleted) or OIDC minting is disabled for this deployment.Treat as non-retryable. Check deployment status.
"rate_limited"429The per-pod mint rate limit was exceeded.Back off and retry. Prefer getOidcToken caching over repeated raw calls.
"timeout"undefinedThe mint request did not finish within 20 seconds.Retry with backoff.
"malformed"undefinedThe socket returned HTTP 200 with invalid JSON, missing token or expires_at, or a body larger than 64 KiB.Retry or inspect runtime logs.
"failed"400, 5xx, or undefinedAnother HTTP error or socket transport failure.Check status. HTTP 400 means fix the request or declare the audience in hosting.oidc.audiences; 5xx errors are retryable.

When you request an audience that is not listed in hosting.oidc.audiences, the socket returns HTTP 400 and getOidcToken throws OidcTokenError with code: "failed" and status: 400. Branch on code and status rather than matching reason, which can change.

Call the identity socket directly ​

Use the local Unix domain socket directly from shell scripts, non-JavaScript tools, or when you need a nonce claim (which getOidcToken does not accept).

The socket path is in $CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET, defaulting to /run/cursor/api.sock. Send POST /v1/tokens/oidc with Content-Type: application/json (maximum body size 4 KB):

bash
curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body \
  --unix-socket "${CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET:-/run/cursor/api.sock}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"aud":"sts.amazonaws.com"}' \
  http://localhost/v1/tokens/oidc

Request fields:

  • aud (required string): exact audience declared in hosting.oidc.audiences.
  • nonce (optional string): opaque printable ASCII string with no spaces, up to 512 characters, echoed into the JWT nonce claim.

Success response (200 OK):

json
{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Ii4uLiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "expires_at": 1785500000
}

expires_at is the token expiration in Unix seconds and matches the JWT exp claim.

An undeclared audience, a Cursor-reserved audience, an invalid aud, or a sub_claim field returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error object whose error string can change.

See Cloud Agents OIDC tokens for the full socket HTTP status code table and per-pod rate limits.

Token claims ​

Tokens are signed with RS256 and include alg, kid, and typ: "JWT" in the header. Every Agent SDK token carries these claims:

ClaimValueNotes
isshttps://api.cursor.comSame issuer as Cloud Agents.
subagent_sdk_deployment_id:<deployment-id><deployment-id> is the deployment public ID (asd_ followed by 32 lowercase hex characters).
audRequested audience stringAlways a single string matching an entry in hosting.oidc.audiences.
iatUnix secondsIssued-at time.
nbfiat - 5Allows 5 seconds of clock skew.
expiat + 300Valid for 5 minutes.
jtiUUIDUnique token ID per mint.
agent_runtime"agent_sdk"Identifies an Agent SDK deployment token.
nonceOptional stringPresent only when sent on a raw socket request.

Configure an AWS IAM trust policy ​

  1. In AWS IAM, add https://api.cursor.com as an OpenID Connect identity provider with sts.amazonaws.com as an audience (if your AWS account does not already have one).
  2. Declare "sts.amazonaws.com" in hosting.oidc.audiences and hosting.egressDomains, then deploy your agent.
  3. Find your deployment's exact sub claim (agent_sdk_deployment_id:asd_<32 hex chars>). You can read sub from the JWT payload of a minted token during initial setup. Redeploying the same slug keeps the same deployment public ID; deleting and recreating a deployment generates a new one.
  4. Attach a trust policy to your IAM role that pins both api.cursor.com:aud and api.cursor.com:sub with StringEquals:
json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/api.cursor.com"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "api.cursor.com:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
          "api.cursor.com:sub": "agent_sdk_deployment_id:asd_3f9c0a7b1d2e4f60a9b8c7d6e5f40312"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

Never replace the sub value with a wildcard such as agent_sdk_deployment_id:*. A wildcard trusts every Agent SDK deployment on Cursor.

Verification, rate limits, and trust model ​

For OIDC discovery (https://api.cursor.com/.well-known/openid-configuration), JWKS (https://api.cursor.com/keys), JWT signature verification steps, and per-pod rate limits, see Cloud Agents OIDC tokens.

Keep the deployment trust boundary in mind when scoping external roles:

  • Any code or tool running inside the deployment pod that can reach the identity socket can mint tokens for any audience declared in hosting.oidc.audiences.
  • The platform sets sub from the deployment identity, so one deployment cannot impersonate another.
  • Tokens represent the deployment as a whole, not a single session, tool, or end user. Grant the external role only the permissions that the deployment should hold.
